descriptionChirho: A figurative narrative or comparison placed alongside a truth to illustrate it; the primary teaching method of Jesus in the Synoptic Gospels. Used for individual parables (Matt 13:3, 18, 24, 31, 33, 34; Mark 4:2, 10, 13, 30, 33, 34; Luke 8:4-11; 12:16, 41; 13:6; 14:7; 15:3; 18:1, 9; 19:11; 20:9, 19; 21:29) and for the genre collectively. Multilingual translations are semantically invariant: Spanish 'parábola/parábolas', Hindi 'दृष्टान्त/दृष्टान्तों', Arabic 'مَثَل/أَمثَال', Korean '비유/비유들', Swahili 'mfano/mifano'. The singular (S73799) and plural (S73800) represent grammatical number variation of one lexical sense — an illustrative story or comparison.
